The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Account pages failed for some shoppers
Why, in plain words: A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: at least 9m 19s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 39.0% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): at least 6,142.30 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: refused to act on a suspected cause - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person - not taken
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #540 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Account pages failed for some shoppers
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 02:55 UTC, not back to normal by 03:04:19 UTC
Status: Draft. 0 of 7 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 03:24:59 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:02:27 UTC
Ended by: Argus: escalated to a person, Nov 11, 2026, 03:04:19 UTC - PR #540, opened as a draft

Summary
The service broke at 02:55 UTC and was not back to normal by 03:04:19 UTC, at least 9 minutes 19 seconds later. 30.0% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.0% before it began. At its worst, 39.0% failed. So far, the shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by at least 6,142.30 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. A setting that adds a monthly spending summary to account pages came on, and nothing Argus read records who or what turned it on; the summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month. Argus handed the incident to a person. Argus did not test the first candidate it formed (C1): the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #540, for a person to review and merge. While monthly-spend-feature stayed on, account pages could keep failing for shoppers who had bought before but not this month, and the flag could be switched again without showing up in any change record Argus reads.

Impact
at least 9m 19s - since onset, still not back to normal
39.0% - peak error rate
3,606 - requests failed
1.0% to 30.0% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
at least 6,142.30 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With monthly-spend-feature on, `render_spend_summary` calls `average_spend_per_item_this_month` (as long as `use_typical_spend` is false). That function divides the account's total for this month by the number of its purchases marked `in_current_month`. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has none, so the division is by zero and their account page request raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed.
  Evidence:
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 8 minutes, 02:55–03:02
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 occurrences in 37 minutes, 02:26–03:02; # was 0.50% to 34.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 02:56
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47. That error first appears in the logs at the onset and nowhere before it.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 The monthly-spend-feature flag began evaluating on. Every evaluation logged during 02:25–02:54 UTC was off. At 02:55 UTC some evaluations were on, and the logs show it on during 02:56–03:02 UTC. The switch appears in no change record Argus read: the production change events returned 0 changes, and the flag provider's history showed 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus. What switched the flag is not in the record. No deploy or other change was recorded, so none could be ruled out by the service being measured healthy with it in place.
  Evidence:
    G7e5d INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:25–02:54
    G971b INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 174 / on 26 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:55
    Gce95 INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:56–03:02
    T8 03:02:47 Investigator Agent: Read back 0 production changes
    T14 03:02:50 Argus: Read the flag provider's history - 0 flag changes by anyone but Argus, the 1 hour before 03:02:50
  Ruled out:
    A rollout still under way: the Investigator Agent read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name.
      T9
why 3 Turning the flag on sent account pages for shoppers with no purchases this month down a code path that divides by their number of purchases this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
    G5309
Contributing factors
- The switch of monthly-spend-feature to on was not recorded in the production change events or the flag provider's history, so Argus had no recorded change it could undo and refused to act on C1. (AI-3, AI-4)
- The alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it. (AI-5)
- No test was seen that exercised the flag-gated monthly summary for a shopper who has bought before but not this month before the flag was turned on. Code-Fix reports that the existing tests call this shopper the ordinary case and their own helper builds one. (AI-6)
- The flag went from on for part of traffic to on for all of it, and no guard was seen that held or reverted it while the account page error rate rose. (AI-7)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | The monthly-spend-feature flag was switched from off to on at about 02:55 UTC. This enabled the spend summary path, which raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 and fails roughly 30% of account page requests. No deployment, config change or rollout split is recorded. | 0.93 | never tried: the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person

Trigger
No trigger was established.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
 | 03:02:56 | Refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person | Argus | nothing to put back | not taken
 | 03:04:19 | Proposed a fix: PR #540 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 02:55 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 03:02:03 UTC, 7 minutes 3 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Review and merge the proposed fix | mitigate | unassigned | PR #540 | open
AI-2 | Turn monthly-spend-feature off for io-shop until the proposed fix is merged and deployed. | mitigate | unassigned | - | open
AI-3 | Find out how monthly-spend-feature was switched on without appearing in the flag provider's history or the production change events. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Make every flag change on io-shop go through the flag provider so it is recorded in the history Argus reads, and close any path that switches flags outside it. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to an on-call page. | detect | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Require tests that run each flag-gated code path with its flag on, including shoppers with past purchases but none this month, before the flag can be enabled in production. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-7 | Make flag rollouts on io-shop stage through traffic slices, and pause or revert automatically when the error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came 6 minutes 3 seconds after its series passed its line, within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute its series is read in.
- 41 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at 02:55.
- 47 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent formed 1 candidate cause, best first: C1.
- 53 seconds after the alert was raised, Argus refused to act on C1 - the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person.
- 2 minutes 16 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #540.
What went wrong
- No mitigation was applied during the response: the flag was still on and account pages were still failing when the incident was escalated to a person.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

Timeline (UTC)
 | Nov 11 02:55 | IMPACT BEGINS | the incident began
 | 03:02:03 | DETECTED | HighErrorRate on io-shop fired
T1 | 03:02:24 |  | Argus Received HighErrorRate on io-shop
T2 | 03:02:30 |  | Argus Moved the incident to INVESTIGATING - a worker took the incident up
T3 | 03:02:38 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's per-minute metrics, anchored on 03:02:03

T5 | 03:02:44 |  | Investigator Agent Placed the start of the incident at 02:55
T6 | 03:02:45 |  | Investigator Agent Recorded where the 3 replicas run - all on Tesla-V100-SXM2-16GB
T7 | 03:02:46 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 02:56
T8 | 03:02:47 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 0 production changes
T9 | 03:02:47 |  | Investigator Agent Read how far the deployment had rolled out - all 3 replicas run one revision, which the history does not name
T10 | 03:02:48 |  | Investigator Agent Asked for the service's log lines, the 37 minutes 3 seconds before 03:02:03
T11 | 03:02:48 |  | Investigator Agent Read back 133 log lines

T19 | 03:04:19 |  | Argus Moved the incident to ESCALATED - a draft pull request is open at PR #540

Response effort
none - engineer time
151,550 - tokens spent by Argus

Supporting information
The incident's walk: http://localhost:8000/incidents/84dadec4-9f46-48a6-9e5f-92a1b9b39109
The fix it proposed: PR #540 (https://github.com/ohadraz/Argus-Demo-Target-App/pull/540) opened as a draft. The record holds nothing about it after that.
Changes to production read
Deploys read, none came back; flags read, none came back.
Log messages read (UTC)
G7e5d | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off - 200 evaluations - 30 occurrences in 30 minutes, 02:25–02:54
Gad41 | INFO io-shop: account pages rendered normally - 6 occurrences in 23 minutes, 02:25–02:47
G46bc | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection - 43 occurrences in 37 minutes, 02:26–03:02
Gbac1 | WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 32 occurrences in 37 minutes, 02:26–03:02; # was 0.50% to 34.50%, typically 1.50%, highest at 02:56
G971b | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=off 174 / on 26 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 02:55
G5309 | ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 14 occurrences in 8 minutes, 02:55–03:02
Gce95 | INFO io-shop: monthly-spend-feature=on - 200 evaluations - 7 occurrences in 7 minutes, 02:56–03:02
What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month divides account.total_this_month_cents by len(bought_this_month), the number of the account's purchases that have in_current_month set. A shopper who has bought before but not this month has no such purchases, so the function raises ZeroDivisionError. tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py calls that kind of shopper "the ordinary case", and its own helper builds one. render_spend_summary calls this function whenever use_monthly_summary is true and use_typical_spend is false. So turning on monthly-spend-feature made every idle shopper's page in that slice fail, which is the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 that the investigation found. Turning the flag off hid the error but didn't remove it.

The fix: if nothing was bought this month, the function now returns 0 (nothing spent per item this month) instead of dividing. The return type stays int, so render_spend_summary and its callers in src/io_shop/account_page.py get the same kind of value as before. Shoppers who did buy this month take the same arithmetic as before.

What's unchanged: the lifetime average_spend_per_item still raises for an account with no purchases at all. The existing tests in test_spend_summary.py and test_account_page.py depend on that: they check that the error reaches the request boundary, and that the reported line contains //. That function sits above the one I changed, so its line numbers don't move. The edit adds no try/except, so other failures still propagate as before.

The tests: two new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py. One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month for a shopper with past purchases but none this month and expects 0. The other goes through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True) for the same shopper and expects 0. Against the current code, both would raise ZeroDivisionError at the division.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

Review checklist
✓ Key incident data collected (met)
○ Impact assessed (for a person)
  the loss is measured to the close; when the service is back to normal is for a person to report
○ Root-cause analysis complete (for a person)
  the change the candidate names is not in the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person; running the proposed fix's tests against the current code would confirm Code-Fix's reading, not that the code it reads is what ran (AI-1)
○ Every action item owned and dated (for a person)
○ Reviewed and shared (for a person)

The document, by field:

The summary's code likely fails when it works out an average for shoppers who have bought before but bought nothing this month. Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. No one was paged, so no on-call responders were called in. Argus did not undo the suspected change because that change is missing from the record of what changed, so undoing it is left to a person. Argus also opened a proposed fix, PR #540, as a draft. The fix has not been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
